mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month MAs simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals robust demand expansion, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND HOUST > 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during two consecutive months when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 12-month MAs.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during three consecutive months with UNRATE above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon: higher-than-expected monthly RSAFS growth is associated with higher short-term equity returns, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS growth surprises and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample testing.
